children: Malaysian palm oil futures rose on Friday, buoyed by gains in rival edible oils on the Dalian and Chicago markets, with the contract on track for a third straight weekly gain.

The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for January delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange gained 20 ringgit, or 0.42%, to 4,812 ringgit ($1,178.69) a metric ton by the midday break. The futures are set to post a 0.9% weekly gain.

The advance was "supported by gains in CBOT soyoil and firmer crude oil prices. Strength in the soy complex was driven by follow-through buying after robust US export sales data and easing harvest pressure," said Cheang Kang Wei, a Singapore-based analyst at StoneX brokerage.
Crude oil prices rose on Friday after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns of further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 2.15%, while its palm oil contract
gained 0.56%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were up 0.6%.
Palm oil tracks rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

Brazil's soybean exports are expected to fall 0.8% to 113 million metric tons in 2027 from the year prior, crushers group Abiove said on Thursday, as stronger domestic processing demand limits supply to importers such as China.

Crude palm oil prices are expected to stay above 4,600 ringgit ($1,128) per metric ton in November on stronger export demand, sustained biodiesel consumption and a seasonal decline in production, the Malaysian Palm Oil Council said on Thursday.
Palm oil (FCPOc3) may retest a support at 4,736 ringgit per metric ton, as a correction from 4,852 ringgit looks incomplete, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said.
